report.answer_text:
A typical horizontal-jib tower crane uses three motions to place a load: the hoist moves it up and down, the trolley moves it toward or away from the tower, and the slewing unit swings it around the tower. (morrow.com)
| Part | Function |
|---|---|
| Base and foundation | Support the crane and transfer its weight and lifting forces to the ground. A fixed-base crane is typically anchored to a concrete foundation. |
| Mast (tower) | The vertical steel framework that gives the crane its height and supports the upper assembly. |
| Slewing unit (turntable) | Rotates the upper assembly, including the jib and counter-jib, around the mast. |
| Jib (working arm) | The long arm that provides horizontal reach and supports the trolley. |
| Trolley | Travels along the jib to move the hook closer to or farther from the mast. |
| Hoist winch and wire rope | The winch winds or unwinds the rope to raise or lower the hook. |
| Hook block | The hook-and-pulley assembly where the load’s slings or other lifting gear attach. |
| Counter-jib | The shorter arm opposite the working jib. It supports the counterweights and often carries the hoist machinery. |
| Counterweights | Offset the turning effect of the working jib and suspended load, helping keep the crane stable. |
| Operator’s cab and controls | Give the operator a place to control and monitor the crane’s movements. |
These are the main parts of a typical fixed-base, top-slewing crane; layouts vary by model. (morrow.com)
A luffing-jib tower crane changes its reach by raising or lowering the angle of the jib rather than moving a trolley along a horizontal arm. (liebherr.com)
